name: 麺屋 一麺専心 (Menya Ichimen Senshin)

claims.text: A wheat-noodle ramen shop with no gluten-free offering; wheat noodles are boiled throughout the kitchen, so cross-contamination is unavoidable.
The menu includes a special shoyu (soy sauce) ramen; standard ramen shoyu tare is wheat-based, and no wheat-free tare is indicated.
All bowls are animal-based, a pork-bone tonkotsu and a chicken paitan, and even the complimentary warmed vegetables come out of a meat-broth kitchen.
Bowls are built on wheat noodles and a fish/shoyu base; the shoyu tare is the standard wheat-containing type with no gluten-free alternative mentioned on any source.
All broths use animal stock (dried sardine, bonito, kombu, clam, chicken) with chicken oil and pork chashu; no vegan or vegetarian bowl exists, so shared pots make any vegan accommodation impossible.
Single small 10-seat counter kitchen built around wheat ramen noodles; no separate gluten-free preparation is advertised, so cross-contact with wheat is effectively unavoidable.
Tare/seasoning composition is not published; standard ramen tare typically contains wheat-based soy sauce, so assume wheat unless the shop confirms otherwise.

Although the dashi itself is animal-free (kombu, iriko and fish flakes), it is fish-based and the bowl is topped with pork chashu; no plant-based bowl is offered, so the kitchen is not set up for vegan service.
Cooking is explicitly 無化調 — no chemical seasonings, yeast extract or preservatives — which some additive-sensitive diners value, though this does not make it gluten-free or vegan.

The broth is unusually a 100% seafood dashi (no pork or chicken stock), which is relevant for diners avoiding meat/poultry stock specifically — but it still contains fish and the bowl includes pork chashu.
All bowls use house-made wheat noodles boiled in shared water, with sesame dan dan sauce or chicken broth and (typically) wheat-based soy sauce tare; there is no gluten-free preparation.
Japanese ramen tare for chicken/shoyu-style bowls is normally made with wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
The kitchen is chicken-based throughout (chicken paitan broth, minced-chicken and chicken-chashu toppings, egg), so vegan cross-contact is unavoidable.

name: 麺や高倉二条 (Menya Takakura Nijo)

claims.text: Wheat ramen/tsukemen noodles are the core of every bowl and are boiled in shared water; no gluten-free option exists, so cross-contamination is unavoidable for celiac diners.
Bowls are seasoned with a soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in Japanese ramen is typically brewed from wheat-containing soy sauce.
All broths are animal-based (15-hour pork-bone stock plus fish dashi); there is no separate vegan preparation, so any item would contact pork and fish stock.

name: 麺屋 やまひで 京都聖護院店 (Menya Yamahide Kyoto Shogoin-ten)

claims.text: Maze-soba tare is built on a soy-sauce-based savory seasoning, which in Japan is overwhelmingly brewed with wheat; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
Signature bowl is topped with spicy minced pork and raw egg yolk, and the alternate house bowl is a chicken paitan; the kitchen is animal-broth and meat based throughout.
Core dishes use wheat noodles and wheat-based Chinese seasonings; high cross-contact risk in a shared noodle kitchen.
The sesame cold-noodle dare and Chinese dishes are very likely seasoned with wheat-containing soy sauce; no allergen breakdown is published.
Kitchen is pork/ham-centered (roast pork, ham cold noodles); animal products are pervasive.
Wheat ramen/tsukemen noodles are the base of every bowl and the kitchen handles wheat flour for the mackerel tatsuta-age topping, so flour and gluten are present throughout the cooking surfaces.
All broths are fish-based (mackerel and kombu dashi); there is no vegan broth, so no vegan bowl is possible even setting cross-contact aside.
Broth is completely additive-free (無化調) using only kombu and mackerel, with no chemical seasonings, fish powder, or animal/pork products - and the kitchen keeps salt low for a lighter, cleaner bowl.
